title: Minkä maalaisia: asking about several people's nationalities
focus: For several people, use minkä maalaisia and a plural olla form: Minkä maalaisia te olette? Minkä maalaisia te olette? — Olemme suomalaisia.
targetSkills: Minkä maalaisia: asking about several people's nationalities
prerequisiteSkills: Minkä maalainen: asking about one person's nationality

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “What nationality are you?”  Address a group (te).
exercises.explanation: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern. The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description. The genitive is a relationship form; in these question phrases minkä means of what or which. For several people, use minkä maalaisia and a plural olla form: Minkä maalaisia te olette? (“What nationality are you?” addressed to a group). Minkä itself does not change. The complete question means “What nationality are you”.
requiredSkills: Minkä maalaisia: asking about several people's nationalities
exercises.targetSkill: Minkä maalaisia: asking about several people's nationalities

parts.formation: Olla has the plural you-form olette: ole- + -tte.

exercises.prompt: Answer “Minkä maalaisia nämä opiskelijat ovat?”: choose “These students are Estonian.”
exercises.explanation: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern. An ordinary plural description uses the plural partitive nationality form: Me olemme suomalaisia (“We are Finnish”). In the taught -lainen words, -lainen becomes -laisia: suomalainen → suomalaisia. A group addressed as te replies with me or omits it with olemme. Keep he when both speakers refer to the same other group. The complete reply means “These students are Estonian”.

exercises.explanation: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern. An ordinary plural description uses the plural partitive nationality form: Me olemme suomalaisia (“We are Finnish”). In the taught -lainen words, -lainen becomes -laisia: suomalainen → suomalaisia. A group addressed as te replies with me or omits it with olemme. Keep he when both speakers refer to the same other group. The complete reply means “Those students are Swedish”.
